<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **74** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d9e184ab6d83c5160bab0f2b01635517e838ae5` — the merge of head `9e745a06078553d2d8410f3b6af52b68f21bf307` into base `2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d9e184ab6d83c5160bab0f2b01635517e838ae5 && git checkout 7d9e184ab6d83c5160bab0f2b01635517e838ae5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 9e745a06078553d2d8410f3b6af52b68f21bf307 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 && git merge --no-ff 9e745a06078553d2d8410f3b6af52b68f21bf307

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat check

**L1: REWORK, one item** (L1-a, for the #35786 card thread) at head `683dd62a94441c8bcfd597cdfa2dfe677ef91232`, read 2026-11-20T11:57Z. Everything else below is accepted as read. After the fix, a delta L1 and a CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS on the final head are owed. The L2 is at that tier because `packages/spec/src/**` is touched; a Clause-② TIER_DEFAULT review is not enough.

### Owed: a fixed-read leaf refused at the door is not logged

ADR-0155, on the refusal (line 468): "**The refusal** is ADR-0139 D3's envelope **wherever it occurs**: status 500, `INTERNAL_ERROR`, a message naming the evaluator, the leaf and the remedy, **logged at `error` once per evaluator**". The changeset repeats it: "Anything else is refused before any driver is asked, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, logged at `error` once per evaluator."

On this head that holds only at the executor boundary:

- `passFixedReadLeaves` wraps `collectFixedReadLeaves` in a `try` and calls `logRefusalOnce(…, flagOf(host.facade), 'evaluator')` on an `isFixedReadLeafSeamRefusal`.
- The two **door** calls throw the same refusal with no log: `collectFixedReadLeaves(object, operation, node, path)` in `filter-comparand-shape.ts`, and in `engine-top-level.ts`'s lowering ("refused here by name, before the doors below").
- `git grep isFixedReadLeafSeamRefusal` finds the one catch, in the seam.

The door runs first, so a leaf out of position or on the wrong verb in a caller's `where` (wrong field or object, `$nin`, a list member, `having`, a delete) is refused **unlogged**. Only a leaf that reaches the boundary, such as one a `beforeFind` hook wrote, which your pin at `engine-fixed-read-leaf-seam.test.ts:318` covers, is logged. You flagged this yourselves, and it is a gap against the ADR and the changeset, not a style point: the log is how an operator finds a composition fault that the caller only sees as a 500.

**Fix.** Route the door's throws through the same once-per-evaluator log, with the same flag keyed on the engine (`flagOf(facade)`), so a door refusal and a boundary refusal together log once. For example, catch and log around the two door calls, as the seam does, or move that catch into `collectFixedReadLeaves`' callers through one helper. Then add a pin: a caller's `where` with a misplaced branded leaf is refused 500 and logged once at `error` across two calls.

Narrowing the changeset sentence instead would leave the code out of line with ADR-0155's "wherever it occurs", which changing would need an ADR amendment. Don't take that route.

### Accepted as read

- **Declarations.**
  - `Clause-②: yes` (widening only): new `DriverCapabilities.fixedReadLeaves`, new spec and core exports, and the door admitting a branded leaf.
  - `Metadata-protocol: added`, per claim amendment 7037678092: the driver capability is on the authorable surface (`authorable-surface/data.json` +1). `@objectstack/spec` `minor` follows.
  - `core` and `objectql` are `patch`.
  - Nothing narrows: an unbranded copy is still refused at the door as a non-list, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, as before.
- **The seam** (`fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`). In order:
  1. the principal check (`isSystem` exempt, else the user or the delegator);
  2. D4's two classes: the object and `sys_record_share` on different datasources, or middleware or a `beforeFind` / `afterFind` registered for the table **by name**;
  3. the driver's `supports.fixedReadLeaves`.

  Each refusal states the remedy. `hookNamesObject` requires both a literal name and dispatch (`hookMatchesObject`), so a global or `'*'` registration stays outside, on ADR-0155's recorded line ("a registration that names no object stays outside the class, and the host is told").
- **Call sites.**
  - The read boundary covers `where`, `having` and each `aggregations[i].filter`, and the composed scopes after composition.
  - A predicate update is judged once, in its write form, for its prior-row read and its write alike (③ ruled A).
  - A delete refuses any leaf ("a share widens edit, never delete", D1).
- **Smaller pieces.**
  - `resolveFilterTokens` returns the leaf by reference, so the brand survives.
  - The two seam modules break the import cycle.
  - `engine.ts` gains +1 at its facade ceiling.
  - `engine-update.ts` and `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts` reach the host through `securityResolversHost`.
- **Prose.**
  - The changeset's other sentences match the code: "No visible change on its own", the declaration paragraph, the seam's conditions list and the core exports.
  - `system-context.mdx` and the three regenerated driver pages match.

### Routing

The card thread lands it itself under `Clause-②: yes` after the delta L1 and the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER PASS on the final head, with CI green there. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35839` decides the route.

## L1 delta: ACCEPT at `9e745a06078553d2d8410f3b6af52b68f21bf307` (2026-11-20T13:27Z)

This delta goes from `683dd62a94` to `9e745a0607`. It has two commits:

- **03f60bf669**, the fix.
- **9e745a0607**, an import move, overlap-check only.

My REWORK 7038939850 is addressed.

### What I checked

- **The device.** `atFixedReadLeafDoor(host, door)` (fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts) runs one door call.
  - If the call throws the seam's refusal, it logs through `logSeamRefusalOnce`, then re-throws unchanged.
  - `logSeamRefusalOnce` calls `logRefusalOnce(err, host.logger, flagOf(host.facade), 'evaluator')`. `passFixedReadLeaves` now calls the same helper, so the door and the boundary key one flag on one engine object.
  - Any other error is not logged by this device. That includes the unbranded copy's `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. ✔
- **Every door call is covered.**
  - The door's two `collectFixedReadLeaves` calls are both inside `lowerWhereFilterArray`:
    - the object branch, through `assertListComparandShapes` at engine-top-level.ts:930;
    - the array branch, direct, at :1061.
  - At the head, every `lowerWhereFilterArray` call in `packages/**/src` outside tests is wrapped:
    - find (engine-find.ts:440) and findOne (:809);
    - count (engine-count-aggregate.ts:116);
    - aggregate `where` (engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:1040) and delete (:188);
    - update (engine-update.ts:207).
  - The only unwrapped call is `judgeWhereAdmission` (engine-top-level.ts:1287), behind `ObjectQL#judgeFilter`.
  - The two direct `assertListComparandShapes` calls are wrapped too: aggregate `having` (:1307) and the per-aggregation `filter` (:1164).
  - The driver-memory function with the same name is a local one in another module. ✔
- **The flag is the same object.**
  - The facets' `facade` is the engine, through the `#30020` host member.
  - count's host is built per call with `facade: this` (engine.ts:5325).
  - `passFixedReadLeaves` reads `securityResolversHost.of(this.facade)`.
  - The shared-log pin is the positive control: a door refusal and a boundary refusal produce one `error` line between them, in either order. ✔
- **The pin** is `describe('[ADR-0155 D4] a refusal at the door is logged on the boundary's flag, once per engine')`. It covers:
  - two refusals giving one log;
  - door and boundary sharing one log, in either order;
  - nine sites, each asserting the 500 envelope, `calls` empty (no driver asked) and exactly one `error` line;
  - an unbranded copy that stays 400, is not logged, and does not spend the flag. The next misplaced leaf still logs.
- **The dev's ablations** are reported as: door logs nothing ⇒ 11 red; own flag ⇒ 1 red. Each one names the face it guards. ✔
- **Prose.**
  - The seam docblock's "## The log" now says the refusal is logged "wherever it occurs" and explains why the door has no logger of its own.
  - The `filter-comparand-shape.ts` docblock names the device.
  - The changeset sentence is unchanged ("refused before any driver is asked, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, logged at `error` once per evaluator"). It is now true at the door too. ✔
- **CI at `9e745a0607`:** 64 success, 14 skipped, 0 red. ✔

### For the L2 (the dev's two notes; I do not block on either)

1. **`ObjectQL#judgeFilter`.** It goes through `judgeWhereAdmission`, which returns the door's refusal as a judgement, runs nothing and logs nothing.
   - ADR-0155 says the refusal is logged "wherever it occurs".
   - The L2 should rule whether a judgement that serves no 500 counts as an occurrence.
   - My reading is that it does not: no request was refused and nothing was served.
2. **`engine.ts` facade ceiling.** It is now at 6854 of 6854. The next card that touches `engine.ts` has no headroom left. That is not a finding on this diff.

### L2 owed

- **CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER PASS on `9e745a0607`** (ADR-0155 step 2). It should judge the device and both notes above.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9e745a06078553d2d8410f3b6af52b68f21bf307`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf.ts + packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-position.ts, packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts, packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-security-resolvers.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-count-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/core/src/utils/fixed-read-leaf-refusal.ts, packages/core/src/utils/readable-ids-driver-refusal.ts, packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #35839 for card #35786 (ADR-0155 plan step 2, the engine seam and the driver declaration). First contract-review round on this PR: no earlier record names it, so nothing is closed by id here.

Read: the card body and every comment on it (the three dev reports and the claim amendment 7037678092 included), the PR body, the 32-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head, ADR-0155 D1, D4 and the execution plan as the card cites them, and the 83 check-runs on the head: 65 success, 18 skipped by their selectors, none red, none pending. Check Changeset (four runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core with shards 1 to 10, and the Type Check jobs are among the green ones. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; code outside the diff was read at the head to judge the files in scope.

The rest of the diff is the lane seat's at `TIER_DEFAULT`: four test files, the three generated driver reference pages, the system-context census row 18f, the three spec baselines, the two ADR-anchor files and the changeset. Row 18f was read because it states the system exemption; it agrees with `passFixedReadLeaves`.

On the two header lines the template carries for other arms: no `hits` path sits under `skills/**`, `ui/skills/**` or `.claude/**`, so neither arm reads them on this PR and no `security` label duty arises from this record. They are answered truthfully all the same. The changed hunks do govern sharing and permission behaviour (whose share-grant scope an engine read may carry, and when it is refused), so the first reads `yes`. No hunk alters what an agent may do without the maintainer, what is done in what order, or what must go to him, and the PR body declares no rule change, so the second reads `none`.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged.

1. **`DriverCapabilities.fixedReadLeaves`, a new optional key** (`@objectstack/spec`): a list whose members are the closed set `FIXED_READ_LEAF_NAMES`, one name today. The accept set widens by one optional list; every existing declaration parses as before; a name outside the set is refused by the schema. The authorable-surface baseline gains exactly `data/DriverCapabilities:fixedReadLeaves`. **Right.** The key's name, the list-of-names shape, absence meaning none, and its landing on this card beside its reader are what the card states as the seat's O1 ruling, and the reader (`driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`) is in the same diff, as ADR-0078 asks.
2. **Three new exports from `@objectstack/spec/data`**: `FIXED_READ_LEAF_NAMES`, `FixedReadLeafName`, `fixedReadLeafNameOf`. The api-surface and export-origins baselines gain these three and nothing else. **Right.** A capability is declared data and a unique symbol cannot be a schema value, so the declaration needs names; the name sits on the one private row that already holds the brand, the guard and the description.
3. **`readableIdsLeaf`**: its describe text gains one sentence on how it relates to the new key; the accept set is unchanged. **Right**, and it is the relation the card asked the two spellings to state.
4. **The conformance case-set**: `FixedReadLeafCaseSet.leaf` is retyped from the literal `'SharedRecordIds'` to `FixedReadLeafName`, the same one-member union today; the seam list grows by 11 cases, all refusals, to 32 (the 13 evaluator cases are untouched). **Right.** The published set only gains cases, and each added case is judged in ④.
5. **`@objectstack/core` gains public exports**: `fixedReadLeafRefusal`, `refuseFixedReadLeafOnce`, `describeFixedReadLeaf`, the type `FixedReadLeafRefusalError`, and `logRefusalOnce`. `refuseReadableIdsOnce` keeps its signature, its line text, its once-only flag and its `error`-else-`warn` sink. **Right.** One envelope and one log device for both leaves is ADR-0155 D4's "built once" row.
6. **`resolveFilterTokens`, `hasFilterToken`, `isFilterObject`** (`@objectstack/core`) now treat a fixed-read leaf as they treat a `ReadableIds` leaf: returned by reference, never walked as a filter object. Before, a token rebuild copied the leaf and dropped its brand. A widening, and the card's first carry-forward. **Right.**
7. **The engine's comparand door** (`@objectstack/objectql`) admits a branded leaf whose brand is in `ENGINE_FIXED_READ_LEAF_BRANDS` as a `$in` comparand. Before this diff every such value was refused as a non-list, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Now a legally placed leaf goes on to the boundary's checks; a branded leaf out of position, on the wrong verb or in the wrong form is refused by name, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500; an unbranded copy is refused at 400 exactly as before. **Right**: D1 and D4 make a misplaced branded leaf a composition fault, never an author's.
8. **`ObjectQL#judgeFilter`** runs the verbs' own door functions, so its answers move with item 7: ok for a legally placed leaf, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 for a misplaced one, where it answered `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. **Right.** No author-written or wire filter can carry the brand, and what the boundary decides (recipient, classes, declaration) needs a context and a driver, which the judge never had.
9. **No new package export, public engine method or error code in `@objectstack/objectql`**: `index.ts` is untouched and both new modules say so. **Right for this step.** Steps 5 and 6 will need a public face for the class recognition and the declaration reader; that is theirs to add and to grade (carry-forward below).
10. **Nothing narrows.** No key is removed, no value accepted before is refused now: the branded leaf was refused before this diff, and where it is still refused only the code moves from 400 to 500.
11. **Holds kept**, each checked in the tree: no boot refusal; nothing outside spec and tests builds a leaf; no driver, plugin or service declares `fixedReadLeaves`; no ADR-0147 anchor case is pinned. At this head every operation carrying a leaf ends in the declaration refusal, and nothing writes one, so there is no visible change. **Right**, and it is what plan step 2 and the card's two holds require.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` at `minor` and `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/objectql` at `patch`. The diff moves the authorable-surface baseline by one new key, which is the kind `added`, and AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives that kind at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. Core and objectql carry no protocol change, and the same step ships a non-protocol change, widening included, at `patch`. **The levels match what the diff publishes.**
- The PR body and the changeset body both carry, line-initial, `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. `yes` with no arm is right: the diff changes a published contract and every change in ① is a widening or a code move on a value that stays refused, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed. The PR body's third line, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, is owed by the `added` kind and its reason holds: no page under `skills/**` teaches driver capability keys.
- Check Changeset is green on all four of its runs on this head.
- The changeset's prose agrees with the tree except for one sentence that is wider than the tree in one spelling (N3 below).

### ③ Boundary flags

**SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** The diff materialises no ids and adds no in-app join. The seam hands the leaf to the driver by reference or refuses the operation; nothing in the diff substitutes an id list for a leaf, and the declaration's own text forbids it. No finding.

**The open question** (first dev report): which `Metadata-protocol` value the PR carries, since the claim spelled `none` and the authorable-surface baseline moved. Answered A by the rule, in the claim amendment 7037678092 and patch round 1: `added`, spec at `minor`. Right, for the reason in ②. Option B, taking driver capabilities out of the authorable surface, is a shape decision of its own and is not owed by this card.

**The dev's flags**, each answered:

1. Leaf names added to spec. Right, ① item 2.
2. Two seam modules instead of one. Right. The door sits below `engine-top-level.ts`, which the class recognition imports for `hookNamesObject`; splitting the filter-only walk out lets the door and the boundary ask one function, with no cycle and no second copy of the position rule.
3. The update and delete facets import `securityResolversHost`, and `engine.ts` grows by two lines to its 6854-line ceiling. The facade gate is green on this head. The arithmetic against #35773 and #34817 is the seat's sequencing and no contract matter; note that merging `main` or either sibling into this branch moves the head, and this record covers `9e745a06` only.
4. A refusal at the door is logged (patch round 2). Right. `atFixedReadLeafDoor` wraps every verb's door call and logs on the same per-engine flag `passFixedReadLeaves` uses, so a refusal at the door and one at the boundary write one line between them. The reading of D4's "once per evaluator" is the driver for a declaration it lacks and the engine for every fault that is the seam's own. Accepted; N4 notes its one cost.
5. `judgeFilter` is not logged; the last report leaves this for this review to rule. **Ruled: no log is owed.** A judgement refuses no operation: `judgeWhereAdmission` returns every door's diagnostic as data and logs none of them, this one included. Its in-tree consumers were read at the head. The CLI authoring judge and the metadata-protocol authoring gate judge author-written filters, which cannot carry a brand. The analytics merges judge a read scope under `aggregate` and wrap a not-ok answer in their own `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` error, whose message is kept for the operator's log; and at this head the analytics merge's own comparand door names no fixed-read brand, so it refuses such a leaf closed whatever the judge answers. The card's Order section gives the analytics entry to step 5, which owns what is logged there.
6. An array-form `in` / `nin` carrying a leaf stays `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 from `parseFilterAST`. Accepted deviation. D4's Admission paragraph lets no caller but the engine's door and the analytics merges admit the brand, and `parseFilterAST` is the spec's standalone lowering, which names none; the `ReadableIds` leaf has the same answer in the same spelling; the array form is request sugar no producer writes a leaf in; the operation is refused either way; and the one array spelling that does lower a leaf by reference (`=`) is refused by name at 500 by the walk this diff adds to the array branch. See N3 for the changeset sentence.
7. `logRefusalOnce` factored out of `refuseReadableIdsOnce`. Checked against the removed lines: the same line text for the default `who`, the same flag set before the write, `error` with the `warn` fallback. Behaviour unchanged.
8. Process items (the PR opened after local verification, the commit trailer pair, the killed and restarted local runs, the relay writes, one rerun of an unrelated flaky shard on an earlier head): no bearing on the contract; the lane seat's.

Nothing is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**The three `hits` files.**

- **`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`**, against the O1 ruling, ADR-0155 D4 and its first consumer, `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`. Each sentence of the key's doc was read against the seam. The leaf reaches the driver only when the list holds its name: true, the consult is the last check and reads `getDriverForObject(object).supports` on every operation, nothing cached, which is the doc's "read at dispatch time". Otherwise the operation is refused before any driver is called, 500, naming the driver, the leaf and the remedy: true of the message `passFixedReadLeaves` builds. Absence means none: true, and so does every malformed value (null, a string, a non-array), because the reader takes only an array that includes the name. A leaf inside a composed `ReadableIds` scope needs both declarations: true, the nested sites are consulted against the outer driver's list and the composed leaf around them is ADR-0139 D3's. The schema is a closed enum over the frozen name list, so `['ReadableIds']` neither type-checks nor parses. The change holds.
- **`packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf.ts`**. The name lives on the one private row that holds the brand, the guard and the description, so the four cannot drift, and `fixedReadLeafNameOf` answers `undefined` exactly where `fixedReadLeafBrandOf` does: the same search over the same guards. The change holds.
- **`packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts`**. The 11 added seam cases, each against D1 and ③ ruled A: the write form on `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`, refused; the write form inside a composed scope, refused, since a composed scope is the `where` of a read of its parent; the leaf as an implicit-equality value, a `$eq` comparand, a `$nin` comparand, a member of a `$in` list, a filter node of its own, and inside a nested-relation condition, each refused as D1's "any other position". All eleven are right. The docblock's new sentence, that the prior-row read of a predicate update is that update's and is judged once, was checked in `engine-update.ts`: the seam runs at the executor's entry, and the prior-row reads and the `updateMany` go to the driver directly with the same AST, never back through `find`'s door, which would refuse the write form. The set's first consumer, the objectql seam test, runs every case against a real engine with a recording driver, and Test Core is green on this head. The change holds.

**The implementing files**, read sentence by sentence against D1 and D4.

- **`fixed-read-leaf-position.ts`**. Position: admitted only at `field.$in` where the field is `id` and the scope's object is the one the leaf names, directly or inside the scope of a composed `ReadableIds` leaf whose parent is that object, at any depth of nesting; `$and`, `$or` and `$not` are descended; every other key, operator and container is scanned and any leaf found there is refused. Verb and form: read form on the four read verbs and inside every composed scope, write form only directly in an `update`'s `where`, neither on `delete`; `having` and an aggregation's filter are refused before anything else is read. This is D1 as written, with ③ ruled A.
- **`fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`**. The recipient rule compares and never replaces; a system context is exempt only when `isSystem` is strictly `true`, and from that rule alone: the position, class and declaration checks run for it too. The two classes: datasource of the leaf's object against the datasource of its inner table, through `resolveDatasourceBinding`; an object-scoped middleware or a `beforeFind` / `afterFind` hook that names the table. Both answer the refusal at this step: for the first class it is the R1 that stands behind R2, for the second the refusal that stands behind the boot check, and R2 and the boot check themselves land with the producer at plan step 6. The refusals are core's envelope, 500, naming the seam, the leaf and the remedy.
- **`filter-comparand-shape.ts`**. The wrapper is the only caller that names the brands, and it runs the position walk first, so a branded leaf in a `$nin` or a list is refused by name before the list-shape door could read it as a caller's 400. Right order, and it is what turns D4's "never `INVALID_FILTER`" into fact at the door.
- **`engine-top-level.ts`**. The array branch of `lowerWhereFilterArray` runs the same walk on the lowered condition. `hookNamesObject` requires the registration to name the object literally and to dispatch for it, so a global or `'*'` registration is outside the class and `excludeObjects` takes an object out, which is D4's boundary.
- **`engine-security-resolvers.ts`**. `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` passes `having`, each aggregation's filter, and the `where`, and on a read that composes `ReadableIds` it passes the composed `where`, so the leaves a security-answered scope carries are judged before the driver sees them. D4's "every occurrence, nested ones included".
- **`engine-find.ts`, `engine-count-aggregate.ts`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `engine-update.ts`, `engine.ts`**. Door calls wrapped for the log; the seam at the executor's entry of `update` and `delete`; two host members added. They agree with the contract.
- **`fixed-read-leaf-refusal.ts`, `readable-ids-driver-refusal.ts`, `filter-tokens.ts`, `index.ts`** (`@objectstack/core`). The envelope is `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 with the evaluator in the message; `describeFixedReadLeaf` names the leaf and its inner table and never its inputs. They agree with the contract.

**Tried against the design, and held.**

1. A driver call that skips the seam. At the head the door's callers are the six verbs and the judge, nothing else. Each read verb's driver call, the aggregate's in-memory fallback read included, takes the AST `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` returned; `update` and `delete` run the seam at the executor's entry, before their prior-row reads.
2. A leaf written after the door, by a middleware or a before-hook. The boundary runs the same walk and every other check on the final AST.
3. Another principal's scope. The leaf guard admits only a non-empty string recipient, so an absent context or a context with no user never compares equal; a third identity under a delegated context is refused; a nested leaf is compared with the same reading context as a direct one.
4. A leaf smuggled inside a composed scope a caller forged. ADR-0139's walk refuses any composed leaf at the door; the only composed scopes the seam descends are the ones the engine built at the boundary, and there the leaf must name the scope's parent and be the read form.
5. Class recognition on an unbound object. `resolveDatasourceBinding` answers the default binding, so two unbound objects compare equal and an object bound elsewhere does not: the compare ADR-0139 D5.3 already makes.
6. A malformed or partial declaration. It reads as none and the operation is refused; no shape of `supports` lets a leaf through unnamed.
7. The brand lost on the way to the driver. The copy-on-write walkers between the door and the driver (the token resolver, the `ReadableIds` composer) return the frozen leaf itself; the pass-through edits nothing.
8. An unbranded copy. Still 400 at the door, not logged by this device and not spending its flag.
9. A principal's id leaking through a refusal. No message built here includes the recipient.
10. Cost on ordinary traffic. The walk throws only on a branded value and answers a shared empty list for a filter with no leaf; it is one more read-only pass per door and boundary call, the same shape as ADR-0139's walk beside it.
11. A silent drop on an `update` by scalar id that also carries a predicate. The combination is already refused before the seam, so no leaf is skipped there.

**Findings.**

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits only; none has an effect on correctness or on the contract at this head, and none is to be fixed in a commit that moves a reviewed file.

- **N1 (nit, the two-leaf shape; follow-up on the card that adds ADR-0147's leaf to the seam).** The seam is built once, as D4 asks, but in three places it fixes the shape of this leaf's answer where the second leaf's differs. The row type `FixedReadLeafRules.position` can only answer one field on the object the leaf itself names; `fixedReadLeafClassOf` takes the class-1 object from that answer; and what the seam answers for the first class and for a driver that does not name the leaf is the refusal, in the body of `passFixedReadLeaves`, for every name. `driver.zod.ts` states that refusal, and "no list fallback", as the key's rule for every fixed-read leaf. D4's "built once" table keeps what an evaluator that cannot run a leaf answers per leaf, and ADR-0147 as it stands (Proposed; its D-a and D-d) puts its leaf on any field of any object and answers both cases with its exact-array floor. Every statement in the tree is true for the one name the list holds today, and ADR-0155's Sequencing note leaves ADR-0147's answer to that record. The card that adds the second leaf widens the row, moves the two answers into it and rewords the describe.
- **N2 (nit, prose face: the PR body).** The body says twice that 12 seam cases are added, 33 in all, and the first dev report says the same. The tree adds 11 and holds 32. The seat corrects the body; the head does not move.
- **N3 (nit, accepted deviation: the changeset).** "Anything else is refused before any driver is asked, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500" is wider than the tree in one spelling: an array-form `in` / `nin` carrying a leaf is refused at 400 (③ flag 6). Left as written; a changeset edit moves the head.
- **N4 (nit, follow-up for the switch card, plan step 6).** One per-engine flag covers every fault the seam itself answers. After the first such refusal on an engine, a later refusal of another kind or for another object writes no line: a host with a second object on another datasource, or a hook added later, is told by the refusal alone. D4's "once per evaluator" is met to the letter and every caller still receives every refusal. Worth weighing where R1 at boot lands, since the class refusals are per object and per host.
- **N5 (nit, doc residue in two `hits` files; fold into the next card that edits them).** The jsdoc of `fixedReadLeaves` names the position, verb and recipient checks ahead of the declaration consult and leaves out the two classes, which the seam also answers first. The header of `fixed-read-leaf.ts` still says the module declares two shared halves, and it now also holds the leaf names.

**Carried forward, not graded.**
